messages:
emma_r: Heads up — customer acme-inc reported a p99 jump on /v1/generate starting ~2026-03-15T09:12Z. They saw p95 ~180ms -> 260ms and p99 ~220ms -> 1.1s. Ticket TICKET-5123. Suspecting continuous-batcher config change pushed last night.

kyla_support: Customer says regressions only for short prompts (<30 tokens). Long prompts unaffected. They also saw some 504s but mostly slow tails. Provided sample request IDs: req_9f3a, req_9f3b, req_9f3c.

sanjay: I pulled metrics — small-prompt QPS up slightly, but batch size distribution shifted toward size 1/2. p99 aligns with timeouts in batcher hold window. Query used: 
```
sum by(route, batch_size) (rate(batch_events_total[5m]))
```
shows spike in batch_size=1 events on prod-east pool.

oliver_sre: Thanks. Which config was rolled yesterday? I saw a deploy at 02:10 UTC from config-service: reduce max_wait_ms from 25 -> 8 for continuous-batcher to lower latency for common paths. That will reduce wait but increase tiny batches. On small prompt workloads that can break amortization and cause tail amplification if CPU scheduling/kv-cache misses happen.

emma_r: Right — the change was intended to help median latency, but we didn't simulate tiny prompt distributions. Customer workload is many tiny requests in bursts.

sanjay: Repro steps I used locally (quick):
```
# short-prompt load
wrk -t4 -c200 -d60s -s tests/send_short.lua --latency http://prod-east.example/v1/generate
```
This reproduces p99 ~800-1100ms when max_wait_ms=8, p99 ~250-350ms when max_wait_ms=25 and batching allowed to accumulate.

oliver_sre: Quick mitigation options:
- Rollback max_wait_ms -> 25 for prod-east (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%)
- Alternative: set min_batch_size=2 for pools handling tiny prompts so singletons get delayed just enough to join a batch
- Per-route routing: route acme-inc to a dedicated pool with conservative batching

kyla_support: Customer needs a fix ASAP. They prefer no rollback if we can avoid it. They're open to a short canary.

sanjay: I'm in favor of targeted canary on the pool serving acme-inc (prod-east-4). Plan: patch continuous-batcher config as follows and canary to 10% of nodes in prod-east: 
```
continuous_batcher:
  max_wait_ms: 25   # revert short wait
  min_batch_size: 2 # avoid singletons
  burst_coalesce_ms: 2
```
Monitor p99, batch_size histogram, and token throughput.

oliver_sre: Also add a short-term guard: if observed p99 > 700ms on a route for 3m, auto-fallback route to a lower-throughput but lower-latency pool (dedicated-small) to keep customer SLA. We have that code path, just needs enabling for this customer.

emma_r: I'll coordinate with infra to run the canary. Deploy-bot will log.

deploy-bot: started canary rollout config continuous-batcher -> prod-east (10% of nodes). change_id cfg-2026-0315-07.

oliver_sre: While canary runs, please collect these traces for any slow requests:
- request_id, batch_size, wait_ms, kernel_ms, kv_cache_hit (true/false), host_id
Example query to extract: 
```
select request_id, batch_size, wait_ms, kernel_ms, kv_cache_hit from request_traces where route='acme-inc' and ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
```

kyla_support: I forwarded the planned canary and repro steps to acme-inc. They agreed to watch and provide feedback.

sanjay: Early canary numbers look promising — p99 dropped from ~1.0s to ~280ms on canary nodes, batch size distribution moved from 55% size=1 -> 20% size=1. Will keep monitoring for 30m then widen.

emma_r: If canary holds for 30m, widen to 50%. If any increase in median or token-cost > 10%, flag here.

oliver_sre: Follow-up action items:
- (sanjay) finish canary and widen, collect traces for failed 5xx and long tails
- (emma_r) notify customer and update TICKET-5123 with mitigation steps and ETA
- (infra) consider a permanent route-level default config to avoid aggressive small-wait for tiny-prompt customers

kyla_support: noted, updating ticket. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary widened to 50% (cfg-2026-0315-07). monitoring alerts enabled.

sanjay: After widening p99 on affected route stable ~260-320ms, singletons reduced. Closing short-term mitigation. Will open a RFC for per-route batching defaults and add synthetic tests to our release checklist to simulate short-prompt-heavy workloads.

emma_r: thanks all — closing slack thread, will add summary to postmortem if customer escalates further.
